push_tactic_snapshot.rationale: Lab/capstone chapter; learner did not re-read the chapter but used its Generation→filter→dedup→verify→selection cascade as the launch point for a full design of their LIVE production system (Lina TMR sales-call synthetic-conversation pipeline). This is the framework-extension-evidence pattern at its strongest — application to a novel real domain. Learner ran hot (frustration mid-session, demanded 'stop asking questions, just answer', swore once) — tactic shifted from Socratic-probe to direct-answer on demand, which is the correct read of a learner who has already done the analysis and wants the expert verdict.

evidence: E1 (★★): Conversation-synthesis = environment-simulation reframe (Q1) — learner observed 'single QA is easy, conversation is hard' and (with teacher) crystallized WHY at the category level: single-QA = i.i.d. point sampling from a distribution; conversation = coherent-trajectory sampling from a coupled dynamical system (two agents + state + dynamics + outcome). A generator that is a *world*, not a *function*. This reframe retroactively explains why the entire session kept collapsing into RL problems — it is the organizing insight of the whole probe and a genuine framework-level synthesis the chapter does not state.

E2 (★★): Actor-vs-controller separation as an invariant (Q2) — across THREE successive learner proposals (give-the-LLM-all-taxonomy → let-it-handle-somehow → rank-by-probability-then-random-pick), teacher identified the single recurring failure: control decisions handed to the LLM inherit the LLM's bias. Learner internalized 'LLM renders, never selects'. Notably, learner correctly CAUGHT a teacher omission — when teacher said ranking buries the tail, learner countered 'but I sample randomly among the top-10, so it isn't always the top' — a valid objection that forced the teacher to sharpen to the precise survivable claim ('the tail is *outside* the top-10 window; randomness can't recover what the cutoff deleted'). Peer-level adversarial engagement, not student-level absorption. Maps to ch-26 [[Q3]] information-asymmetry and ch-27 [[Q11]] verifier-hierarchy.

E3 (★★): 'Influence is an environment property, not a training-stage choice' (Q4) — learner argued the standard, correct SFT/RL division (SFT=coverage+noise, RL=effective selling). Teacher pushed back that 'do influence in RL' does not dodge the problem, it relocates it: if the customer's next state is pre-drawn (action-independent), the RL environment has zero learnable policy gradient for influence — a non-reactive environment defeats RL exactly as it defeats SFT. Learner then refined correctly: SFT can use freewheel+coverage (reactive unnecessary at SFT), RL needs a reactive environment (ch-31 bridge). This is mechanism-level RL understanding (transition-dependence → credit assignment → policy gradient) applied to their own pipeline, and it resolves the frozen-per-round-arc as wrong for BOTH stages.

E4 (★): Context-distillation independent reinvention (Q3) — learner's own design ('inject control instructions during generation, strip ~90% in post-processing, keep a few') WAS context distillation; teacher named it and supplied the literature (Askell 2021 / Agent-FLAN). Learner's instinct ('keep a few so the model still follows instructions') was correct but under-specified; sharpened into scaffold-injects (strip) vs steering-injects (keep = the runtime control channel that still fires at inference). Learner then accepted the compliance-rail boundary (informed_consent/DNC/purchase-recording stay HARD, never distilled — regulatory), recognizing it as the inverse of ch-29's verifier rule (hard gate exactly where correctness is checkable AND mandatory).

E5 (★): Diversity decomposition + deck/hand model (Q5) — learner asked 'how to ensure diversity, this is the real hard part'. Teacher decomposed: surface/persona/concern (combinatorial, already solved by the learner's samplers) vs trajectory/difficulty/outcome (LLM mode-collapses). Learner correctly recognized the deck-vs-hand distinction (taxonomy = population to sample from; one customer = a small coherent hand) and that diversity comes from *different small subsets*, not from everyone-holds-everything. Rejected the 'give the LLM all 120 categories' shortcut after seeing it breaks coherence + diversity + tail-coverage simultaneously.

E6 (★): Head/tail operational definition + 'biased candidate set' (Q6, Q7) — learner pressed 'tell me straight, what is head and tail' (rejecting loose usage). Pinned to an operational test: head = LLM produces well from the label alone (no grounding needed); tail = LLM lacks the content (needs real-example grounding + sampler-forced sampling). Crux internalized: 'a biased candidate set cannot be randomized out of' — selection by LLM-probability is anti-tail by construction; tail must be force-boosted (anti-probability), and the head-heavy LLM prior is exactly why every 'let the LLM choose' mechanism fails.

E7 (★): Taxonomy dual-use + residue-is-treasure (Q8) — learner pointed teacher at their real expanded taxonomy file (gpt-5.4-mini-expanded, 10 families → 48 subtypes → ~240 leaves with definitions/signals/examples). Recognized it serves BOTH generation (leaf examples = few-shot exemplar-grounding, not label-expansion) AND classification/coverage-metering (signals+definition = classifier spec) = ch-26 [[Q7]] eval-as-data-spec. Teacher caught the trap in learner's 'classify then expand' plan: classifying real objections into the *existing* closed taxonomy is a lossy projection that launders the tail into the head; the unclassifiable residue is the most valuable data and must be allowed to *reshape* the taxonomy bottom-up.

E8: Cold-start grounding via human-played logs (Q9) — learner correctly surfaced their real asset: no call transcripts, but logs of humans role-playing the customer against the LLM-TMR, plus human feedback. Teacher's caveats accepted: (a) role-play distribution-shift means trust the objection *content* but not the *frequency* (ch-27 [[Q11]] 'world-minus-one'); (b) the LLM-TMR turns must NOT be cloned as SFT targets (they ARE the old rule-based Lina the learner is trying to escape) — mine the customer side only; (c) the gpt-5.4-mini-imagined leaf examples must be re-grounded with real mined utterances or the grounding is LLM-on-LLM echo.

E9: Trajectory design landed at the right altitude (Q10) — learner proposed building trajectories as Positive/Neutral/Negative first. Teacher sharpened: P/N/U is call-level (1 per call, NOT the dead per-round random-walk), outcome-anchored (P=purchase/N=rejection-DNC/U=defer), and is precisely the *lowest resolution at which intent is checkable against realized outcome* — so the long-deferred verifier (raised turns 1/5/9) finally lives here as intent-class vs realized-terminal agreement. Learner correctly sequenced terminal as a refinement WITHIN the class; teacher added the constraint that terminal must be entailed by the class and any reversal must be path-justified, not stapled.

E10: Meta-skill transfer — how to ask good questions (Q11) — learner stepped out of the domain ('how do I ask good questions, it's hard') and teacher reframed: good questions are harvested from where one's own analysis hit an unresolvable fork, not invented; recipe = belief+reason+break-point+judgment-ask. Learner then asked teacher to co-build the senior-scientist question list FROM their own written core-insight — and teacher demonstrated the skill by extracting 7 forks verbatim from the learner's text. Learner is preparing to take this to a senior scientist: research-practice maturation, not just content mastery.

E11: Self-authored synthesis as the probe's closing artifact — learner wrote their own compressed core-insight ('Diversity under verified dataset; pipeline = Generation→filter→dedup→verify→selection; target = sales call; open Qs: generation strategy, dedup strategy, naturality vs verified trajectory, per-turn response-type selection should depend on TMR → may break interaction'). This independently re-derived the session's central tension (Q1/Q2/Q4) in the learner's own words and correctly flagged the per-turn-response-type-selection fork as the load-bearing one — evidence the framework was internalized, not just followed.
rationale: This chapter was consumed as a capstone *application probe*, not a re-read — the strongest possible mastery signal per the framework-extension-evidence pattern (application to a novel real domain). The learner took ch-29's single-turn Generation→filter→dedup→verify→selection cascade and re-derived, end-to-end, what each stage becomes for multi-turn sales-call synthesis on a LIVE production system, producing six above-bar framework extensions (E1-E7, with E1/E2/E3 at ★★). The organizing insight (E1: conversation synthesis = environment simulation, not data generation) is a genuine generalization the chapter does not state and that correctly predicts why every sub-problem became an RL problem. E2 and E3 show mechanism-level RL reasoning (actor/controller bias inheritance; transition-dependence → policy gradient) applied to the learner's own architecture. E3 is the standout interaction: the learner caught a real teacher omission (random-sampling-among-top-10) and forced a sharpening — peer-level adversarial engagement. E4 (context distillation, independently reinvented and correctly bounded by the compliance-rail seam) and E7 (taxonomy dual-use + residue-is-treasure, grounded in the learner's actual 240-leaf file) tie abstract frameworks to running code. Cross-chapter retention is dense (ch-25 Q9/Q12, ch-26 Q3/Q4/Q7, ch-27 Q11/Q15, ch-28 Q6 all invoked and correctly applied). The meta-skill turn (E10) and the self-authored synthesis (E11) show the learner maturing from content-mastery toward research practice — converting analysis into senior-scientist questions and naming their own load-bearing uncertainty. Real gaps (all correctly triaged as out-of-scope-for-now, not failures): the reactive RL-time customer simulator (deferred to RL / ch-31); sim-to-real transfer measurement (named by teacher as the learner's largest unaddressed risk); end-model evaluation (named as the weakest link to bring to the senior); concrete dedup implementation on trajectory-skeletons (principle established, not built). These are exactly the questions the learner is taking to a senior scientist — appropriate triage, not gaps in understanding. Discuss-equivalent depth reached entirely within the application probe; no separate Discuss phase per standing directive.
